processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h before hot rolling.
Ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples; samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching. This is the parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq.
Solution-treated samples were aged at 650 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching. This defines the sample (process_id proc_aging-650c-1h, state 650°C-1h).

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 15Al alloy at 650 °C for 1 h the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn (α → β-Mn transformation), with abundant fine new precipitates present within the β-Mn; combined with the EBSD results these precipitates are BCC and FCC phases. The SE-SEM panel for this condition (650 °C − 1 h) shows an essentially uniform transformed matrix with a fine 'New precipitates' detail in the inset.
structures.number_of_phases: 3 (β-Mn, new BCC phase, FCC Cu-rich phase)

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn / at β-Mn interfaces

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (for this 650 °C/1 h sample the α matrix had almost completely transformed to β-Mn with fine BCC and FCC precipitates).
interfaces.interface_notes: Detailed TEM characterization of the β-Mn/FCC Cu-rich interface (FCC twins, FFT confirmation) was performed on the 15Al 600 °C/6 h and 17Al 575 °C/6 h samples (b0057, b0058), not on this 650 °C/1 h sample; only the general interfacial precipitate description applies here.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester at a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the value given by the average of 5 measurements.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load of 9.8 N for 15 s; 5 repeated measurements per sample, average reported
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy after aging at 650 °C for 1 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: 857.1 ± 15.4 HV obtained after aging at 650 °C for 1 h; hardness at 625–650 °C stabilizes between 800 and 900 HV with prolonged aging time.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE imaging, 50 µm scale bar with 10 µm inset (electrolytically polished surface)
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) in the 15Al alloy after different aging treatments, including the 650 °C − 1 h panel
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 650 °C − 1 h condition the matrix is essentially uniform/featureless with a fine 'New precipitates' detail visible in the 10 µm inset.

unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy, the fracture toughness K_IC = 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 and the average indentation crack length of 18 µm were measured on the peak-hardness sample (965.6 HV, 600 °C/6 h), NOT on this 650 °C/1 h sample; they are not attributed to this sample.
The nanoindentation average hardness (11.7 ± 0.4 GPa) and the intrinsic β-Mn hardness (12.1 ± 0.3 GPa) for 15Al were obtained on the hardest sample (600 °C/6 h), not on this 650 °C/1 h sample.

The β-Mn volume fractions attributed to specific aging conditions (85.8 % at 525 °C/3 h; 3.9 % for FCC Cu-rich + BCC at 650 °C/3 h) belong to other aging conditions of the 15Al alloy, not to this 650 °C/1 h sample.
